A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Self-Cross diffusion-guidance research. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary materials are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-generation comparisons, quantitative SD1.4 results, a patch-aggregation ablation, and supplementary SD2.1 examples.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds SD2.1 and SD3 quantitative evaluations, three-subject synthesis, spatial-relation tests, and an alternative-loss case study.

M1.justification: The core aggregation and overlap loss remain, but v2 adds an SD3 adaptation using image-image and image-text attention with maximum fusion of CLIP/T5 attention maps (Appendix A). It also introduces CONFORM+Ours, applying CONFORM early and Self-Cross later during SD2.1 generation (Section 5.2). These extend the actual inference procedure.

E1.justification: The original datasets remain, with the 31-prompt Similar Subjects Dataset renamed SSD-2. V2 adds SSD-3 with 21 three-subject prompts and evaluates T2I-CompBench's 2D-Spatial and 3D-Spatial subsets. These introduce additional subjects and explicit spatial-relation requirements.

E2.justification: V1's SD2.1 comparison includes vanilla SD2.1 and Self-Cross only. V2 Tables 3 and 5 additionally evaluate INITNO and CONFORM in that setting, alongside CONFORM+Ours. The original SD1.4 comparator set and supplementary Attention Refocusing comparison remain.

E3.justification: Added evaluations introduce SD3-medium, quantitative SD2.1 comparisons, the spatial-relation metric Rel, and an SSD-3 evaluation comprising 21 prompts and 1,365 images per method. The retained sampling description still specifies 50 steps with Self-Cross guidance during the first 25; the additions do not establish that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix B and Figure 9 add a Self-Self alternative-loss case study examining image concatenation and its attention maps. The existing one-patch/16-patch/masked-patch ablation, CLIP-score reliability checks, and failure examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 65 images per prompt and matched random seeds across methods. V2 introduces no new repeated-run procedure, confidence intervals, variance estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial SD3 and SD2.1/spatial results in Tables 1, 3, and 5. For example, SSD-3 existence scores are 33.54 for SD3-medium and 57.92 for Self-Cross; no-mixing scores are 70.08 and 77.15. These are new comparisons, while the original SD1.4 and Attention Refocusing numerical results remain unchanged. Figure 4 drops the bear/elephant and bus/truck example rows.

T1.justification: V2 adds Equation 9 defining SD3 cross-attention through the elementwise maximum of CLIP and T5 attention maps. The original aggregation and pairwise overlap mathematics remain; replacing the generic pair count with an explicit binomial count clarifies the existing formulation. No new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The central claims about training-free Self-Cross regularization, reduced subject mixing, and multi-patch aggregation remain. The introduction expands the stated benchmark contribution to include both two-subject and three-subject prompts.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies the attention-separation rationale to selected timesteps and layers and explains why relationship tokens remain unconstrained. It acknowledges dependence on Attend-and-Excite's effectiveness on SD2.1 and warns that missing subjects can inflate no-mixing scores (Section 5.2 and Table 5). Appendix B adds a background-separation explanation for Self-Self concatenation artifacts.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly documents SD2.1's 24-by-24 attention maps, normalization for larger maps, and SD3 attention extraction and fusion. Several existing sampling details are relocated there. Conversely, v1's disclosure of a single RTX4090 with 24 GB memory and batch size one is omitted.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to T2I-CompBench, T2I-CompBench++, pseudo-numerical diffusion sampling, and Enhancing MMDiT-Based Text-to-Image Models for Similar Subject Generation. The central related-work positioning and novelty argument remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 extensively edits the abstract, introduction, method explanation, and experimental discussion. It reorganizes the formulation around pairs and multiple subjects, consolidates implementation details and CLIP discussion in the appendix, and integrates the former supplementary SD2.1 material into the main narrative.

P2.justification: V2 adds three tables and figures covering SD3 examples, multimodal attention, and Self-Self artifacts. It reduces Figure 4 from four prompt rows to two, moves the existing SD2.1 gallery into the main paper, relocates CLIP displays to the appendix, and substantially resizes and rearranges displays.

improvement.justification: V1's broad applicability claims relied mainly on SD1.4 quantitative results and selected SD2.1 examples. V2 substantially strengthens their assessment through SD2.1/SD3 comparisons and three-subject/spatial tests, while exposing backbone-dependent weaknesses and explaining an alternative loss's failure. These gains improve both support and qualification of the central claims. Missing evaluation prompts for the new spatial/three-subject settings and removal of hardware details limit reproducibility but do not outweigh those improvements.
